column3: “Both yesterday and three days ago” is rendered “In times past,” and “ruler” as “prince.”
“By the hand of Samuel” is rendered “through Samuel.”
NASB puts “that is, Jebus” in parentheses.
“People called it” is rendered “it was called.”
“Went continuously and becoming great” is rendered “became greater and greater,” and NASB adds “for.”
“Held strongly with him” is rendered “gave him strong support.”
The written Hebrew reads “chief of the officers” (or “of the thirty”); NASB has “chief of the thirty.” “Wielded his spear” is rendered “lifted up his spear,” and NASB supplies “whom he killed.”
The Hebrew “He delivered a great deliverance” is rendered “saved them by a great victory.”
“Craved” is rendered “had a craving,” and “Who will give me” as “Oh that someone would give me.”
“By their lives” is rendered “at the risk of their lives,” and NASB supplies “who went.”
The Hebrew reads “chief of the three” and “a name with the three”; NASB has “the thirty” both times, as in the Syriac. NASB spells “Abshai.”
“More than the three by the twofold” is rendered “Of the three in the second rank”; the Hebrew is difficult. NASB adds “first.”
“Two Ariel of Moab” is rendered “the two sons of Ariel of Moab.”
“The mighty men of the strengths” is rendered “the mighty men of the armies.”
